title: The 30-minute reset and the operator check
purpose: Every phone restarts on time, and a bad cycle is caught and fixed on the floor.

steps.do: Restart every phone that did not restart.
steps.detail: Walk all ten in the same order. Tap start on any still stopped.
steps.check: All ten record a new cycle.

steps.do: Check each phone's last cycle: start, middle, end.
steps.detail: Three things: hands and the work in frame, enough light, real work done.
steps.check: You know which phone had what wrong.

steps.do: Look for the eight fraud patterns.
steps.check: You can name the pattern, or say none.

steps.detail: Refit the rig, reset the angle, move the wearer into the light. Say the rule again.

steps.do: Check battery and storage on every sweep.
steps.detail: Not enough for the next cycle, or a storage warning, means a spare now, on the wearer's own account.
steps.check: The wearer log has the swap.

steps.do: Write every fault on the device sheet.
steps.detail: Device number and time. Swaps, storage warnings, who you corrected and why, a slipping rig.

steps.do: Treat the 4:00 PM buzz as the end.

done: All ten record on the right head, every fault is fixed or swapped, and written down.

fails.then: Check the app and the account. Still nothing: swap in a spare, tell the Portfolio Manager.

fails.if: Idle or hat off while recording
fails.then: Say the rule again and write it down. That footage still gets a flag.

fails.if: Screen filmed, covered lens, or looped footage
fails.then: That is deliberate. Tap stop, take the phone, call the Portfolio Manager now. Immediate termination.

fails.if: A wearer will not follow the cycle
fails.then: Tap stop, take the rig, tell the Portfolio Manager the same hour. It means removal from the site.

escalate: Your Portfolio Manager the same shift; now for under 18 or no ID; no reply in 20 minutes, call Moharam.
